title: A contractor put someone else’s license number on his business card

beats.text: The license number on the contractor’s business card belonged to someone else.

visual.sub: A business card carried another contractor’s license

beats.text: The customer made a verbal construction agreement in January 2018.

visual.kicker: A business card carried another contractor’s license

beats.text: The prosecutor said the contractor took an excessive deposit.
The report leaves the size of that deposit undisclosed.

visual.kicker: A business card carried another contractor’s license

beats.text: Employees worked without workers’ compensation insurance.

visual.kicker: A business card carried another contractor’s license

beats.text: The prosecutor filed several charges in January 2019.

visual.kicker: Two counts ended in misdemeanor guilty pleas

beats.text: In October, Jackson pleaded guilty to two misdemeanors.

rows.label: Fraudulent use of a license number

beats.text: One count concerned the missing insurance.
The other was fraudulent use of a contractor’s license number.

visual.line: Fraudulent use of a license number

beats.text: The prosecutor reported that Jackson paid $1,200 in restitution.

visual.label: State and City records agree on $1,200 in restitution

beats.text: California’s insurance regulator records the same amount.
It lists two days in jail and 24 months of probation.

visual.kicker: State and City records agree on $1,200 in restitution

beats.text: The records identify no payment by the City.
